questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Both academic opportunities and the culture was important to me. A good university like Monash was high on the list and that the spoken language in the country was english. This is so i could the most out the studies and understand as much as possible so the language would not be a barrier for learning about a different law-system. It was also important to me that is was a country that was different from Denmark and Europe so i could explore a different culture on the other side of the world. Also travel opportunities in the country during my exchange was important

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Only because i still need my final grades for one course it is 9 instead of 10.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
It was a bit difficult in the beginning, but as soon as you knew the system they uses on their university it was easy to find information. 
Information about housing and such was also easy to get to.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received som help on how to choose and plan my courses so it added up without overlapping eachother.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Some of the orientation was a bit unnessescary, but good with some additional non-mandatory events.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
It was a bit difficult in the beginning because it was expensive and a lot was places were really bad, but there is many places to look for housing, such as flatmates and
realestate.au
.
I recommend that you see the housing first and maybe book and airbnb the first 2 weeks of arrival.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is expensive, but so is the on campus housing, I recommend to live some other students, maybe other exchange students. And i recommend living in the city even though your campus it outside of the city

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: a lot of student housing in student houses with small apartments is binding for at least 6 months, which you dont need, so that will make more expensive or you will have to rent it out in the end of the period.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Easy

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We needed to meet at the campus, take a little card with our name on, and then listen to an orientation lecture, and the registration was done. This was really easy, and you met some of the other students as you were sitting in mixed tables and needed to have some chat with eachother during the presentation.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could get help with social issues - if you where nervous or anxoius. You could also get help with your courses, if you didn't know courses you wanted or couldn't figure their system online.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: pretty succesful only a few were filled up, the hardest part was to get it matched up so nothing was overlapping, but it got sorted out before the first courses started.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: You don't have to figure out every course you want before hand as you can still change ypur choice in the first week.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Good, but some courses was without any group work so it was a lot like lectures, and the outcome of the classes could have been better with more student-work in groups or individually.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
My courses was post-graduate - you could only take my courses if you finished your BA already
It was first year of my master - but i think you ciuld take the courses no matter how long you were on your masters/postgraduate programme.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was pretty much the same, the difference was that in some courses there was less group work, and no big lecture with more than 50 student (only in small classes)

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
The Law of Climate change 
Privacy and surveillance 
Discrimination and human rights at work.
Australian legal proces and research.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
The law of climate change!!! 
if you want and overall knowledge of the legal system in Australia i recommend 'Australian legal proces and research' it was a good beginner course.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All kind of clubs, different sports lik running, swimming, football and so on. I think there was bookclubs and such as well.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I didn't use the universities clubs or facilities, but i have heard really good of the fitness and sauna on campus in Clayton.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
I recommend going to Sydney or Queensland if you have more than 3-4 days of - i also really recommend the Great Ocean Road.
I recommend visiting Victoria market for groceries and souvenirs and Fitzroy market for
second.hand
shopping. i also really recommend the NGV and the botanical gardens during their lightshow in july/august.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: easy - it is close to the danish culture - city was much bigger than any danish cities tho. - a lot of people from around the world so very international-

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: talk to them in your short breaks during classes

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Many people - way more laid back than Denmark and also really welcoming. A lot of focus on aboriginal culture and racism. - more than Denmark

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: They are really friendly

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Enjoy that you can learn new things out in the world - its a really good university with good teachers. 

You can get help from the teachers and university anytime you need - so ask for help if you have questions about anything. 

Talk to other students and go on trips when you don't have classes.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Personally I think its a good idea to check the exam-method in the different courses, so youll have as many exams in a way that you prefer so you dont get stressed about it. 

I preferred assignments as you could do them while traveling.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
Traveling and experience the different parts of Australia, because the different places in the country are very different. 
And learning in another language than your preferred languange

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Writing long assignments in english and to live with 'strangers'

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
